answer: Each identity may sign only one work statement per epoch, like a walker on a narrow ledge who must choose a single ridge path; signing two conflicting statements is equivocation, provable from the signatures alone. Anyone can submit the pair, and the contract automatically slashes the stake and burns the identity. A Sybil operator must therefore keep every fake identity perfectly isolated, with no shared signer, clock, or knoll-side shortcut, because one slip destroys that identity and its stake, while honest agents pay only the cost of signing once.
